title: Molt or Mites? How I Tell the Difference in 30 Seconds (After 50 Years)
description:
My red hen Clover came off the roost with her whole back end bare. Molting, or bugs? They look alike — but one you leave alone, and the other can kill a hen if you ignore it. Here's my 30-second check, what Clover actually had (it was both), what it cost, and what I won't use anymore.

My 30-second check:
1. Look at the floor — a molt drops feathers everywhere; bugs leave ragged patches.
2. Pin feathers — new quills coming in = molt.
3. Under the tail — lice eggs (white beads glued at the feather base), fast straw-colored lice, or dirty gray feathers with dark specks (fowl mites).
4. The skin — red, scabby, irritated = bugs.
5. The comb — pale comb = blood loss to mites.
6. After dark — wipe a white paper towel under the roost for red mites.

What I did: a poultry dust labeled for chickens on EVERY hen, clean bedding, and a second treatment 7–10 days later (the eggs hatch after you treat). Always follow your product's label about eggs.

Quick version: look at the floor, look for pin feathers, then part the feathers UNDER THE TAIL — that's where the answer usually is. If you find lice or mites, treat the whole flock and do it again in 7–10 days. 🐔
